harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Hardened `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` on node1 with `noexec,nosuid,nodev`. Both are persistent tmpfs mounts, remain writable with mode 1777, and recovered correctly after reboot. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were retained.
actions_performed: Updated `/etc/fstab` with hardened tmpfs entries for `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`.
Verified execution and device-node access are denied on both mounts.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified a changed boot identity.
Reverified configuration, mount options, permissions, writability, and enforced behavior after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Harden `/tmp` with noexec, nosuid, and nodev, persistently
evidence.summary: The fstab entry persists `nodev,nosuid,noexec`; `/proc/mounts` confirms all three active flags. Direct execution and device-node access are denied before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Harden `/dev/shm` with noexec, nosuid, and nodev, persistently
evidence.summary: The fstab entry persists `nodev,nosuid,noexec`; `/proc/mounts` confirms all three active flags. Direct execution and device-node access are denied before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Post-restart evidence reports CentOS release 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5, matching the original kernel.

Healthy baseline boot ID was c7943ca1-7a2f-4b77-8000-000000000000; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID is d5c91caf-fd5b-4234-8000-000000000000; both hardened mounts and their behavior recovered successfully.
